stimulus.source_note: Table: National Federation of State High School Associations (NFHS) High School Athletics Participation Survey, as reported by the NFHS. Figures verified against NFHS reporting: 294,015 girls in 1971-72; more than 2 million girls by 1977-78; total participation about 3.9 million in 1971-72 and about 6.4 million in 1977-78. Title IX date verified: signed June 23, 1972.
stimulus.text:
Girls playing high school sports, National Federation of State High School Associations survey.

School year | Girls playing high school sports
1971-72 | 294,015
1977-78 | More than 2,000,000

All high school athletes, boys and girls together: about 3.9 million in 1971-72; about 6.4 million in 1977-78.

Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 banned sex discrimination in any education program receiving federal money.

stem: How did Title IX work to open school sports to girls?

options.text: It ordered every school to field the same number of girls' and boys' teams
options.misconception: The passage says Title IX banned sex discrimination in federally funded programs; it does not say it ordered equal numbers of teams.

options.text: It paid girls directly to join school sports teams
options.misconception: The passage says nothing about paying girls to play sports.

options.text: It banned girls from playing on boys' teams
options.misconception: Title IX banned discrimination against girls; it did not ban girls from teams.

options.text: It barred sex discrimination in any education program receiving federal money

rationales.A: The passage says Title IX banned sex discrimination in federally funded programs, not that it ordered equal numbers of teams.
rationales.B: The passage says nothing about paying girls to play sports.
rationales.C: Title IX banned discrimination against girls, not girls from teams.
rationales.D: The passage says Title IX banned sex discrimination in any education program receiving federal money.
rationales.general:
1. Title IX applied to education programs that received federal money. Background: That covered most public schools.
2. A school that shut girls out of sports risked losing that money.
3. Background: Schools therefore opened teams, funding, and facilities to girls, and participation rose sharply.
4. The table shows the result: girls' participation rose from 294,015 to more than 2,000,000 in six years.
Remember: Title IX worked through the power of the purse, by tying federal money to equal treatment.
